evidence_quotes.quote: B2B IDR 354.93 billion; total group revenue IDR 2.25 trillion [from annual report revenue breakdown per channel]

claim_detail.claim: IHC (Pertamina Bina Medika) FY2023 total group revenue IDR 5.72 trillion; +14.9% YoY; 75 hospitals, 68 clinics
claim_detail.note: Two secondary sources (news article + corporate PR). Revenue figure confirmed by spot-check (IDR 5.72T, +14.9%). However: IHC is not publicly listed so no audited filing is available to the public. Indonesia Business Post is secondary-news, Pertamina press release is secondary-press-release. Two secondary sources = Medium by rubric only if ≥1 is from primary category or 3+ secondary. Two secondary from different families is Medium by strict rubric (2+ sources with neither primary). HOWEVER: the hospital count (75 hospitals) is disputed — spot-check found 36 hospitals, not 75. This factual discrepancy in a key figure downgrades to Low pending resolution.
flags: DISCREPANCY: draft claims 75 hospitals; spot-check (Indonesia Business Post + Pertamina news-release data) shows 36 hospitals as of December 2023. IHC had 36 hospitals not 75. Possible confusion with total beds or total facilities (hospitals + clinics = 104). Score Low pending resolution.

sources: Siloam 2023 Annual Report PDF from stockbit/IDX (primary-filing, SILO.JK)

However, this is a directly audited corporate filing — the highest-quality source category. Scored Medium as single primary-filing (more weight than single secondary). Borderline Low/Medium — scored Medium given filing quality.

flags: Direct Kemnaker JDIH portal link for Permenaker 02/1980 would upgrade to High: https://temank3.kemnaker.go.id/page/perundangan_detail/60/

claim_detail.claim: Malaysia DOSH OHD registration requirement under USECHH 2000; 1,113 OHDs registered nationally as of 2016
claim_detail.note: Two sources from DOSH official government portal (primary-ministry). Note: 2016 figure is now 10 years old — outdated-source flag applies but the claim is about regulatory framework (USECHH) + 2016 baseline, not a current 2024 count. The structural constraint point is valid even with old data.
flags: Outdated-source caution: 1,113 figure is from 2016. No post-2016 OHD count cited. The growth since 2016 is unquantified.

evidence_quotes.quote: In 2016, there were 1,113 Occupational Health Doctors registered with the Department across the country. Selangor had the highest number of Occupational Health Doctors with 331 people.

claim_detail.claim: Indonesia had ~65,000 medical specialist shortfall as of 2023; OHD as narrow specialty
sources: en.antaranews.com news article on specialist training (secondary-news)
claim_detail.note: Two secondary sources. Spot-check found the correct 'specialist shortage' narrative is confirmed but different figures: Kemenkes stated 31,481 deficit; IDI cited 47,454 existing vs. 78,000 needed (~30,546 gap). The 65,000 figure in the draft does not match spot-check findings (actual figures from multiple news sources range from 29,000–31,481 deficit). This is a potential factual inaccuracy in the specialist shortage magnitude. Additionally, the 65,000 figure links general specialist shortage to the narrow OHD specialty without specific OHD-supply data. Score Low for factual-dispute on the 65,000 number.
flags: FACTUAL DISPUTE: Spot-check finds Indonesia specialist deficit ~31,481 (Kemenkes source) or ~30,546 (IDI estimate). The 65,000 figure cited in the draft is not confirmed by government sources. This specific figure needs verification against Kemenkes 2023 data.

flags: Geography context: this study was conducted at Peking University First Hospital (China), not in Indonesia or Malaysia. The F1 benchmark is applied as a general technical benchmark, not a SEA-specific measurement.

structural_observations: FACTUAL ERRORS FLAGGED: Three claims have potential factual inaccuracies that should be corrected before the draft advances: (1) IHC hospital count — 75 vs. 36; (2) Indonesia specialist deficit — 65,000 vs. ~31,481 (Kemenkes); (3) Peka B40 NCD rate — 41% vs ~70% (2024 data from MOH). These are the most important corrections needed.

ASSUMED-TAG DENSITY: 18 ASSUMED-N tags across both Stage 2 drafts. This is appropriate given the operational specificity of the claims, but 5 of these feed directly into pain point cost estimates (ASSUMED-1, ASSUMED-3, ASSUMED-4, ASSUMED-13, ASSUMED-14). All cost figures in PP2.1, PP2.2, and PP2.4 are partially assumed and should be labelled clearly in final output.

SOUTH KOREA PROXY FOR CDM FOLLOW-UP: The 22.6% CDM follow-up rate (PMC 12021225) is the single most important quantified claim in PP2.3 and it comes from a South Korean company, not Malaysia or Indonesia. The draft applies it as a proxy without flagging the setting difference (Samsung Electronics Kiheng onsite clinic has 22 dedicated healthcare staff vs. typical MY/ID corporate MCU with no onsite clinic). This is a significant geography + setting mismatch for a foundational claim.

VENDOR-MARKETING IMPROVEMENT vs. STAGE 1: Stage 2 is somewhat better than Stage 1 at flagging vendor self-promotion sources, but still cites prodiaohi.co.id, bookdoc.com, protecthealth.com.my, and doctoranywhere.my in contexts where vendor-marketing override applies.

NHMS 2023 WELL-EVIDENCED: The Nature Scientific Reports paper (s41598-025-08311-9) on NHMS 2023 is an excellent primary-academic source that was identified by the research team. The NHMS 2023 claims are the best-evidenced quantitative claims in this stage.

SINGLE-PREPRINT DEPENDENCY CONTINUES: arXiv 2512.05381 (SATUSEHAT 8.9% FHIR adoption) is cited again in Stage 2 (PP2.2-a context, PP2.1-k). The structural dependency on this single unreviewed preprint identified in Stage 1 persists here.

CONFIDENT OPERATIONAL CLAIMS WITHOUT SOURCES: Several operational workflow claims in Sub-steps 2a–2d (manual scheduling via WhatsApp/Excel being standard; no standard API for HR-to-MCU integration; SATUSEHAT lacking a dedicated MCU module) are stated as facts without sources. These are plausible but need at minimum 1 trade-press or vendor confirmation source.
gate_reasoning: Stage 2 scores 13% High / 23% Medium / 63% Low — materially better than Stage 1 (6%/14%/80%) due to the use of audited corporate filings for Prodia (PRDA.JK) and KPJ (IAR 2023) and the identification of the Nature Scientific Reports NHMS 2023 paper as a primary-academic source. The core pain point logic for PP2.1 (OHD sign-off bottleneck), PP2.2 (multi-lab collation), PP2.3 (CDM follow-up gap), and PP2.4 (scheduling friction) is structurally coherent and defensible. Three factual errors require immediate correction before shipping: (1) IHC hospital count (75 vs 36), (2) Indonesia specialist deficit (65,000 vs ~31,481), (3) Peka B40 NCD rate (41% vs ~70%). For deep-research targeting: the highest-priority upgrades are (a) direct fetch of WHO Malaysia RM 9B NCD productivity loss source to upgrade PP2.3-e to High, (b) Kemenkes specialist shortage primary source to resolve the 65,000 vs 31,481 dispute, (c) MOH KKMNOW Peka B40 dashboard to resolve the 41% vs 70% NCD rate, and (d) IHC pertamedika.co.id for facility count correction. The South Korean semiconductor study proxy for CDM follow-up rates (PP2.3-a: 22.6%) is a structural limitation — a SEA-specific corporate MCU CDM follow-up study would substantially strengthen PP2.3.
